title: Compact dg modules are retracts of finite-cell modules
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $C$ be an associative unital dg algebra over $\mathbf Z$, with $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b)$. Use the left dg modules and their derived category $D(C)$ of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization] on a point; all small coproducts are represented by direct sums of dg modules. Let $M\in D(C)$ be compact [def-pc-compact-object], meaning that $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(M,N_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,\bigoplus_iN_i)$ is bijective for every small family. There is a dg $C$-module $P$ with a finite filtration $0=F_{-1}P\subseteq F_0P\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_tP=P$ by dg submodules whose successive quotients are finite sums of integer shifts of $C$, and maps $M\xrightarrow{i}P\xrightarrow{p}M$ in $D(C)$ with $pi=1_M$. The zero module is allowed. No boundedness, commutativity, flatness or countability hypothesis on $C$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09R3 (proposition-compact), implication (1) to (2), for left modules by the graded opposite algebra.

proof.text: Pass explicitly to right modules. Put $A=C^{\mathrm{opp}}$, with $a*b=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$ and the same differential. A left module $L$ becomes a right $A$-module by $x*a=(-1)^{|x||a|}ax$. Associativity follows since $(x*a)*b$ and $x*(a*b)$ both equal $(-1)^{|x||a|+|x||b|+|a||b|}ba x$; the right Leibniz rule follows by expanding $d(ax)$. The inverse is $ax=(-1)^{|x||a|}x*a$, with the same underlying complexes. For a degree-$r$ left graded map, $h(ax)=(-1)^{r|a|}ah(x)$ becomes $h(x*a)=h(x)*a$, so chain maps and chain homotopies correspond exactly. Thus the two inverse operations induce inverse functors on the homotopy categories and on the localization words defining $D(C)$ in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. They preserve direct sums and cohomology. The shifted left action is $a\cdot_{L[k]}x=(-1)^{k|a|}ax$; hence the converted shifted right action has exponent $(|x|-k)|a|+k|a|=|x||a|$, exactly the unchanged right action on $L^{\mathrm{opp}}[k]$. The regular left $C$ converts to the regular right $A$. Filtrations, quotients, and retractions are unchanged on underlying complexes, and the identical Hom and coproduct maps preserve compactness. It therefore suffices to prove the right-module assertion for the image $E$ of $M$.

source.place: Tags 0FQ0, lemma-left-right, and definition-opposite-dga; section-shift (the sign formulas and their inverse are written out).

proof.text:
Represent $E$ by a right dg module and apply [lem-sfb-dg-property-p-resolution]. This gives a quasi-isomorphism $R\to E$ and an exhaustive filtration $0=F_0R\subseteq F_1R\subseteq\cdots\subseteq R$, with each quotient a small direct sum of integer shifts of $A$. Identify $E$ with $R$ in $D(A)$; compactness is unchanged because precomposition with this isomorphism identifies both sides of its defining bijection. The dg category $D(A)$ is triangulated by [lem-sfb-dg-derived-admissible-triangles]. Apply [lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle] to the inclusions $v_m:F_mR\to F_{m+1}R$. The degreewise colimit is $R$ by exhaustiveness. We obtain
$$ B\xrightarrow{t=1-s}B\xrightarrow{b}E\xrightarrow{\delta}B[1],\qquad B=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}F_mR,\quad s\iota_m=\iota_{m+1}v_m,\quad b\iota_m=j_m,$$
where $j_m:F_mR\to E$ is the inclusion into $R$ followed by the identification.

source.place: Tag 09R3, first paragraph of (1) implies (2); Tags 09KP and 0CRL supply the resolution and the specified telescope triangle.

proof.text: The degreewise shift gives $B[1]=\bigoplus_m(F_mR)[1]$. By compactness [def-pc-compact-object], write $\delta=\sum_{m\in I}\iota_m[1]\delta_m$ with $I\subseteq\mathbf N$ finite and set $\delta_m=0$ outside $I$. Consecutive composites in the twice-rotated distinguished triangle vanish by [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact](i); thus $t[1]\delta=0$ (the rotation sign does not affect zero). Applying the projection onto $(F_0R)[1]$ gives $\delta_0=0$. Projection onto $(F_mR)[1]$ for $m>0$ gives $\delta_m-v_{m-1}[1]\delta_{m-1}=0$. Induction gives $\delta_m=0$ for all $m$, whence the finite-sum formula gives $\delta=0$. This argument uses the forward telescope shift $F_mR\to F_{m+1}R$ and imposes no bound on the degrees of $R$ or $A$.

source.place: Tag 09R3, vanishing of the telescope connecting arrow; derived.tex Tags 0146 and 0149 for consecutive composites and Hom exactness.

proof.text: Rotate the telescope once, obtaining $B\xrightarrow b E\xrightarrow0 B[1]\to B[1]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact](ii), applied to $W=E$ and $a=1_E$, there is $r:E\to B$ with $br=1_E$. By compactness [def-pc-compact-object], write $r=\sum_{m\in J}\iota_m r_m$ for a finite subset $J\subseteq\mathbf N$. Choose $N\geq m$ for all $m\in J$ (take $N=0$ if $J$ is empty), and let $v_{mN}:F_mR\to F_NR$ be the iterated inclusion. Set $a=\sum_{m\in J}v_{mN}r_m:E\to F_NR$. Since $j_Nv_{mN}=j_m$, we have $j_Na=\sum_{m\in J}j_mr_m=br=1_E$. Thus the identity already factors through a single finite filtration stage; we have not asserted that the cells in that stage form a finite set.

source.place: Tag 09R3, splitting and second use of compactness; derived.tex Tag 0149, applied to the rotated triangle.

proof.text: The module $T=F_NR$ has a finite filtration by $F_0R,\ldots,F_NR$, preceded by zero; its quotients are the small sums of shifts from the property-(P) filtration (the initial zero layer is an empty sum). Apply [lem-sfb-dg-compact-map-finite-subcell] to the compact source $E$ and $a:E\to T$. It gives a dg submodule $P\subseteq T$ and $i:E\to P$ such that $(P\hookrightarrow T)i=a$, with a finite filtration $G_kP=F_kR\cap P$ whose quotients are finite sums of shifts of $A$. Set $p:P\hookrightarrow F_NR\xrightarrow{j_N}E$. Then $pi=j_Na=1_E$. Applying the inverse sign conversion of step 1 gives the required left dg $C$-module and the two derived maps for $M$, with the specified filtration and the same retraction equation. Empty layers and $P=0$ are permitted throughout.

source.place: Tag 09R3, final application of Tag 09R2 in the proof of (1) implies (2); Tag 0FQ0 for the explicit inverse sign convention of step 1.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09R3, proposition-compact, implication (1) to (2); with Tag 09R2 and the explicit left/right conversion of Tag 0FQ0.
